key_insight: In laser–TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel, higher laser power deepens penetration, faster welding reduces weld dimensions, and higher current widens the weld while stabilizing the arc.
engineering_relevance: These parameter–response relationships can guide weld geometry and arc stability control for Invar tooling used in aerospace composite manufacturing.
method: Numerical simulation of molten pool dynamics
High-speed photography of molten pool evolution and arc behavior
Parameter variation: 5–6 kW laser power, 0.5–0.8 m/min welding speed, and 150–170 A current
evidence_signal: Within the studied ranges, higher power intensified flow and promoted arc deflection, higher speed increased flow velocity and cooling rate, and higher current strengthened convection and improved arc stability.
watch_item: Trends apply to the tested parameter ranges; the abstract does not report quantitative simulation–experiment agreement or weld mechanical properties.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
